about: The Gospel of the formulary “Nativity of Saint John the Baptist” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Elizabeth’s time to give birth had come, and she bore a son. And her neighbors and kinsfolk heard that the Lord had shown His great mercy toward her, and they rejoiced with her. And it came to pass that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were calling him by his father’s name, Zechariah. But his mother answered and said: Not so; he will be called John. And they said to her: There is no one among your kindred who is called by this name. And they were making signs to his father, asking what he wished him to be called. And asking for a writing tablet, he wrote, saying: John is his name. And they all marveled. And at once his mouth was opened and his tongue loosed, and he spoke, blessing God. And fear came upon all their neighbors; and all these things were being reported throughout all the hill country of Judea. And all who had heard them laid them up in their heart, saying: What, do you think, will this child be? For indeed the hand of the Lord was with him. And Zechariah his father was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying: Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, because He has visited and brought about the redemption of His people.

ex.w116: The subject is omnes, all who had heard. The understood object refers to the things just reported. In corde suo gives where they were laid up.
